info.title: XTen Stack API
info.description:
The HTTP JSON API of XTen Stack (stack-internal.xten.au) and its modules. It is the contract that agents (Cowork, Code, Gemini, Codex, Tim, Watson, Lin), games and sites use. Everything here is generated from `docs/openapi/` in the app_skeleton repository: one part file per area under `parts/`, merged by `bin/build-openapi.mjs`.

## Authentication
- **API key (agents, services, sites):** send `X-Api-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys belong to a Stack user; the user's roles decide what the key may do. A key is the caller's whole identity: a session cookie sent with it is ignored, and a key that does not resolve is `401`. Keys come from Infisical (`xten-secrets`), never from chat or files.
- **Session cookie (browsers):** sign in at `/api/session/login` (or the backend). Session endpoints refuse a request that carries a key.
- **Public** endpoints say so and need no credential.

## Roles
`admin`, `operator`, `agent`, `charter_agent`, `member`. Each operation states who may call it. A caller without the role gets `403`; no credential gets `401`.

## Errors
Failures are JSON with an `error` string (and sometimes `errors` per field): `400` malformed, `401` not authenticated, `403` not allowed, `404` not found, `409` conflict, `422` validation failed, `429` rate limited, `500` server error (logged server-side). Never retry a `4xx` unchanged.

## Conventions
Timestamps are UTC unless a field says otherwise. Money is in cents unless a field says otherwise. Create endpoints that say "idempotent" return `200` with the existing row when called again with the same idempotency key. Operations marked `x-unverified` were documented from reading the code and have not been exercised against a live system.

## Keeping this document true
A change to an API route, its inputs or its responses updates the matching part file in the same pull request. `node bin/build-openapi.mjs --check` fails when the generated JSON is stale or the document is invalid.

get.description:
Returns a static liveness body. Reached via the generic `/api/:params` route (also `/api/index` and `/api/index/index`); any HTTP method is accepted (no method check). Who: any authenticated caller (any role, API key or session). Unauthenticated callers get 401. Authentication: `X-Api-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; a browser session cookie (from `POST /api/session/login`) is accepted only when no key header is sent. 

Fallback behaviour for the whole module: an `/api/...` URL whose controller or action does not exist (or an action missing a required id segment) is forwarded to `IndexController::notFoundAction()` and, for an authenticated caller, returns 404 `{"error":"Not Found"}` (capital N, unlike the per-record `{"error":"Not found"}`). Unauthenticated callers get 401 first. Any exception escaping an action returns 500 `{"error":"Internal server error"}`.

Body is JSON `{email,password}`; form fields `email`/`password` are accepted as a fallback. On success a session cookie is set and the user payload returned. Failed attempts are audited; once 5 failed logins have been recorded for the same email OR the same client IP in the last 15 minutes, further attempts are refused (password not even checked) with the same 401 body as a wrong password. Only active users can log in. Non-POST returns 405.

Public, unauthenticated, for a static page on another origin (the school form on bioldex.xten.au). What stands in for a login:

A request with an Origin not on the list gets 403 `origin_not_allowed` and no CORS headers. An empty list answers no browser origin. A request with no Origin at all (curl, server-side handler) is taken only while `transactions_public_quote_allow_no_origin` is `1`, otherwise 403 `origin_required`.

- Validation (422 with per-field messages), rate limit (429: at most 5 accepted requests per IP and 2 per email address per rolling hour; refused requests do not count), and the instance must have a default internal entity to issue the quote from (503 `not_configured`).
Every request, accepted or refused, is logged. On success the organisation and contact are found or created in Contacts, a draft quote with one line per item is created (SKUs unknown to the catalogue are added at 0.00 and listed in `unpriced`), and staff (and optionally the requester) are emailed. `reference` is `QR-<draft document id>`; the quote number is allocated when staff post it.
CORS: when the Origin is allowed, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoes it with `Vary: Origin`, methods POST, OPTIONS, headers Content-Type, Accept, max-age 600. `OPTIONS` always answers 204 (CORS headers only when allowed). Body may be JSON (Content-Type application/json, or a body starting with `{`) or a posted form (`items` may then be a JSON string). Answers use `{ok, error, message, errors?}`. `Cache-Control: no-store`. Router accepts only POST and OPTIONS.

post.summary: Public storefront quote submission (bridges into Transactions)
post.description:
Public, unauthenticated. Hands a cleaned request to Transactions' QuoteRequest (same validation, rate limit, draft quote creation and notifications as /transactions/public-quote/create) when that module is installed. Differences from the Transactions endpoint:
- The Origin allow-list only controls whether CORS headers are sent. A disallowed or absent Origin is NOT refused on POST (no 403), and the `transactions_public_quote_allow_no_origin` setting is not consulted.
- Preflight `OPTIONS` answers 204 for an allowed or absent Origin, 403 (empty body, no CORS headers) for a disallowed Origin.
- Field aliases accepted: `name` or `contact_name`; `organization` or `organisation` (falls back to the contact name, then "Direct Customer"); `suburb` for delivery suburb; item `quantity` as well as `qty` (a missing or non-positive qty becomes 1). Items with an empty sku are dropped. `po_number` and `role_title` are not forwarded. A non-empty `website` honeypot answers 200 `{"ok": true}`.
- A QuoteRequestFailed is mapped to 503 only when its `error` is `no_default_issuer` (a key the Transactions module never emits), so every real failure (`not_configured` 503, `failed` 500) is answered 422 here.
- Any other unexpected exception during the bridged intake (for example a database fault) falls through to a standalone fallback that validates email, name and items and answers 201 with a generated `BDX-QR-xxxxxxxx` reference WITHOUT saving anything. The same fallback is used when Transactions is not installed.
Router accepts only POST and OPTIONS.
